top_story_title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: two actively exploited RCE zero-days, CISA KEV deadline 30 September
top_story_summary: On 27 September 2026 Citrix disclosed eight vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. Two of them are critical remote code execution flaws - CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, both rated CVSSv4 9.5 - and both were confirmed exploited in the wild as zero-days before the vendor published. Rapid7 reports that CVE-2026-88771 affects vulnerable NetScaler deployments in their default configuration with no additional product features required, and that Citrix rates its attack complexity as low: reliable unauthenticated RCE against essentially any vulnerable appliance. watchTowr characterises CVE-2026-88771 as a pre-authentication command injection. CVE-2026-88772 is a memory corruption issue; the collected text does not fully state its prerequisite feature, so confirm that detail in the Citrix advisory rather than assuming your build is out of scope.
top_actions: Inventory every NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, including HA pairs, lab and DR units, and record the running firmware branch for each.
Upgrade to the fixed release listed in the Citrix advisory for your version branch - the sources here do not state build numbers, so do not patch from a second-hand version claim.
If a maintenance window is not available today, take internet-facing NetScaler interfaces offline or block untrusted inbound access at the upstream firewall until the upgrade lands.

Assume compromise on any appliance exposed during the pre-disclosure period: hunt for webshells and unexpected files under the web-served directories, new local accounts, and unexplained outbound connections.
After upgrade, terminate all sessions, revoke session tokens, and rotate admin credentials, device certificates, API keys and any secrets stored on the appliance.
executive_summary: Citrix disclosed eight NetScaler ADC and Gateway vulnerabilities on 27 September 2026; CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (both CVSSv4 9.5, RCE) were exploited as zero-days before disclosure.
CVE-2026-88771 works against default configurations with low attack complexity and no extra product features - exposure is not limited to an unusual deployment.
Exploitation has reportedly run globally for weeks and included webshell deployment, so patching alone does not close out the incident: rotate credentials and hunt.
CISA added both CVEs to KEV on 27 September with a 30 September due date and ordered federal agencies to remediate by Wednesday.
No fixed build numbers appear in the collected sources - take the fixed-release table from the Citrix advisory for your version branch.
Check Point published a defensive AI-agent capability with NVIDIA OpenShell; tracked under vendor AI defences, not as a network-device vulnerability.
key_actions: **Citrix** — Apply the fixed release from the Citrix advisory for your exact version branch; upgrade the HA secondary first, then fail over and upgrade the primary.
**Citrix** — Where the upgrade cannot happen immediately, remove inbound internet access to the appliance at the upstream firewall or take the VIPs offline.
**Citrix** — Treat every NetScaler that was internet-facing during the pre-disclosure period as potentially compromised, not merely as vulnerable.
**Citrix** — Hunt for webshells: unexpected or recently modified files in web-served paths, files with mismatched timestamps, and any script not present in your build baseline.
**Citrix** — Schedule the NetScaler upgrade as an emergency change today rather than in the next routine window.
**Citrix** — Confirm your running version against the Citrix fixed-release table before scheduling - the fixed builds are not in this report.
**Citrix** — Record both CVEs against affected assets in your vulnerability register with the 30 September 2026 KEV due date.
**Citrix** — Evaluate and document each NetScaler's internet exposure, as the KEV action explicitly requires.

ai_defenses.solution: Check Point semantic monitoring, in beta integration with NVIDIA OpenShell and the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Judges whether each step an autonomous agent takes still fits the task it was given, while the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform holds the boundary in the infrastructure, outside the agent's reach. Check Point states the monitor's verdict can arrive before the action runs, in under 100 milliseconds.

headlines.title: Zero-Day Exploitation of Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772
headlines.summary: Two critical NetScaler ADC and Gateway RCE flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (CVSSv4 9.5), were exploited as zero-days before Citrix disclosed them.

headlines.title: Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited globally for weeks (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772)
headlines.summary: NetScaler zero-days were used to plant webshells on compromised appliances, with exploitation reportedly running globally for weeks before Citrix disclosed.

headlines.title: Citrix confirms two NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: Citrix confirmed CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are being exploited in attacks and has released security updates for NetScaler.

headlines.title: CISA Says Attackers Are Exploiting Two Critical Citrix NetScaler Flaws Globally
headlines.summary: CISA added both critical Citrix NetScaler flaws to the KEV catalog on 27 September 2026 with a 30 September remediation due date.

headlines.title: Citrix Confirms 2 NetScaler Zero-Days After Admins Pulled the Plug
headlines.summary: Citrix released patches for NetScaler zero-days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 after administrators took appliances offline pre-emptively.

headlines.title: Oh Look, The Foot Gun Went Off Again (Citrix NetScaler PreAuth Command Injection CVE-2026-88771)
headlines.summary: watchTowr Labs describes CVE-2026-88771 as a pre-authentication command injection in Citrix NetScaler, noting the flaw was widely known before Citrix disclosed.
